reason: The observation verifies and the gate does not cover it - but the fix is arithmetically false and regresses two currently-passing assertions, so it fails on 'the fix would make it worse'. VERIFIED TRUE: at 390/768/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440 .b-printLinkUrl sets identically as 'https://timeline.signalstu' / 'dio.ie/s/j7Qm2vK4xR9bT1nL6' / 'yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM', the b.css:1227 comment says what the finding says it says, and interaction-check's 'the link is not cut mid-token' (L1834) asserts only scrollWidth <= clientWidth on the PUBLISH field - no clipping - and says nothing about the print sheet or about where a break falls. So this is not a restated gate. It dies on the fix. FALSE MEASUREMENT: 'https://timeline.signalstudio.ie' is 32 characters, but Geist Mono at 13px with the declared 0.52px --track-data measures 8.33px per character, so the host is 266.25px, not the claimed 211px, inside a 218.4px measure in a 220px column. Set white-space:nowrap as proposed and the host overflows its own measure by 48px (measured scrollWidth 266 vs clientWidth 218) and paints across the gutter into the measure column of the two-column print composition - the 'overflow is a guillotine, never a mid-word slice' class, on paper, in exchange for a soft wrap that hides nothing. 'No geometry moves' is the one thing the fix cannot claim. TWO GATE REGRESSIONS ON THE PUBLISH HALF: simulating the proposed two-block-span split on .b-linkField at 390 gives lines [266, 324, 316, 67] - last line 0.205 of the widest, so 'the link breaks where it can be read @ 390' (L2166, currently passing on a 0.25 floor) FAILS; and because display:block spans put a line break inside the node, window.getSelection() returns 79 characters against a 78-character textContent, so 'the link can be selected by keyboard @ 390' (L2165) FAILS and a hand-selected copy now pastes a URL with a newline in it. That is precisely the selectable-and-typable property an earlier round paid for, undone by the fix meant to protect typing. NO CHEAP VARIANT SURVIVES: keeping the host whole on one line needs 268px in a 220px column; shrinking the link to fit needs ~10.6px type, off the declared ramp that audit.mjs checks; dropping the scheme to get 'timeline.signalstudio.ie' (200px, would fit) fails the passing assertion at L1826 that the printed link starts with 'https://'; and breaking after 'https://' trades the host seam for an eight-character orphan line, which render-b.js:1396 already argues against by name for this exact string. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE PAPER: the full 78-character URL, unhyphenated, case-preserved, nothing clipped and nothing hidden, in three monospace lines of exactly 26 characters each - a deliberate rectangular data block for a string that is transcribed character by character, not scan-read. The invoked 'mid-word clamp' lesson is about truncation that deletes or conceals content; a soft wrap that deletes nothing is not that class creeping back. What remains is a preference about which seam a wrap lands on in an opaque string, and the measure denies it at any price the constraints allow.
